author: Codex socialist_green assessment agent (AI-assisted independent assessment)
changeNote: Completed 240 individually interpreted responses and separate substantive evidence review. User authorised neutral representative doctrinal modelling; no 12Axes answers or scores imported.

metadata.name: Communism
metadata.description: The Marx–Engels higher-phase ideal of common production and provision by need without classes or a coercive state.
metadata.scope: Classless, stateless higher-phase communism, distinct from the transitional workers’ state assessed under Marxism. Questions presupposing permanent states, wage income or private firms are answered literally: rejection of both premises is explicitly recorded as a mixed neutral response, not silently translated into communes or a state-socialist programme. Such midpoints are a questionnaire-fit limitation and must not be described as ideological moderation. No incumbent government is claimed to embody the ideal. This is a representative interpretation, not a questionnaire submitted by adherents. Numeric neutral means a stated mixed/conditional judgement, including rejection of the premise where explained; it is not a claim of measured empirical equivalence. Modern biological and technology items are conditional interpretive judgements where no exact historical position exists; they must not be read as empirical findings or a representative survey of adherents.
metadata.phrase: A classless society with common productive resources and provision according to need, without a coercive state.

sources.title: Critique of the Gotha Programme, Part I (1875)
Socialism: Utopian and Scientific, Chapter III (1880)
Manifesto of the Communist Party, Chapter II (1848)
Socialism, especially ownership, Marxist phases and human nature
Theses on Feuerbach (1845; Engels edited edition)

axes.brief: Class power has disappeared in the higher phase. Democratic participation survives as association, while state office and electoral competition are not permanent defining institutions.
axes.counterEvidence: Abolition of political class rule does not prove support for every representative-state institution. Neutral items mean the ideal chooses neither state-office arrangement; they are not missing research concealed as centrist opinion.

answers.rationale: The ideal supersedes national rulers rather than choosing a permanent electoral tenure system.
Expert rule over society would reintroduce political domination.
Equal participation fits common association although citizenship franchise is a state mechanism.
Executive power against collective decisions contradicts free association.
A permanent party-state electoral contest is neither required nor replaced by incumbent monopoly.
Scrutiny of common resources fits accountable social administration.
Independent state courts and government supremacy are both superseded institutional forms.
Union officials cannot become a new governing class.
Ideological exclusion by rulers would restore coercive class-like power.
Direct social decision-making is compatible with the ideal, but state law and binding citizen repeal are not prescribed.
Sole national authority contradicts associated self-management.
Removable administration is acceptable, while a head-of-government constitutional mechanism is not a permanent commitment.
A ruler cannot invoke continuity to remove collective control.
Recallable administrators are consistent with control by the associated people.
Unaccountable rulers contradict the disappearance of political domination.
A military caste taking political power is incompatible with the end-state.

axes.brief: Engels describes coercive government over persons becoming unnecessary; free development rejects a permanent police apparatus.
axes.counterEvidence: Common coordination and care remain, but courts or police are not renamed as voluntary associations to obtain expected scores.

answers.rationale: Free personal development supports self-regarding choice.
Permanent coercive surveillance authority contradicts the stateless ideal.
Peaceful collective expression should not face state suppression.
Free association requires criticism of common institutions.
Government compulsion of self-regarding health behaviour is not part of free association.
Indiscriminate police records recreate a repressive apparatus.
Coercive police stops are not the ideal’s means of shared safety.
Preventive state restraints would restore government over persons.
Official moral censorship conflicts with free development.
Communication should not require state identity permission.
Suspicionless coercive searching contradicts stateless social freedom.
A state prohibition is not the preferred means of preventing interpersonal harm.
Both state warrants and warrantless state policing presume an apparatus the ideal supersedes.
Common administration should not conceal misconduct from its participants.
Private defensive arms are neither a governing principle nor categorically forbidden in a peaceful classless association.
Unreviewed coercive detention is incompatible with the end of political repression.

axes.brief: National antagonism disappears and personal development remains free. This does not require suppressing all cultural difference.
axes.counterEvidence: The Manifesto expects national differences to diminish. It is not a programme requiring every identity to remain unchanged.

answers.rationale: National cultural supremacy would preserve antagonism the ideal overcomes.
Shared accommodation is welcome, but no permanent government spending machinery is assumed.
Free association does not impose national-cultural conversion.
An inherited foreign identity need not bar membership in common life.
Communication can be organised practically without a national-language hierarchy.
Historical recognition can respect communities without national domination.
State preference for predominant traditions is incompatible with the end-state.
Neither cultural separatism nor national homogeneity should override individual development.
Voluntary shared schedules and plural observances can coexist without state compulsion.
Multiple traditions can coexist, but official national identity is not a required institution.
Participation is desirable while state integration programmes are not the means envisaged.
Community language access facilitates voluntary shared life.
Nation-first family identity conflicts with overcoming national antagonism.
A religious exception and a general clothing prohibition both presuppose coercive law; neither is the ideal.
Several cultural lives can coexist without antagonistic national sovereignty.
State assimilation programmes contradict free social association.

axes.brief: Classless international association rejects coercive state borders and economic exclusion, without making cultural diversity itself an admission test.
axes.counterEvidence: Asylum, passports and visas presuppose states. Modern answers express opposition to coercive exclusion, with explicit qualifications where benefit or residence mechanisms disappear.

answers.rationale: State-imposed settlement caps conflict with the end of coercive borders.
Moving to meet human needs is compatible with international association.
Skills selection contradicts membership and provision by need.
Shared family life should not be separated by borders.
Protection should not depend on productive skills or cultural fit.
No coercive migration illegality should bar residence, though the illegal-status category itself disappears.
National labour-market exclusion has no place in the end-state.
Common production should meet housing needs without national exclusion.
A national quota cannot determine family unity in a stateless association.
Movement is free, but wage-employer job offers cease to structure admission.
People need no employer or family sponsor’s permission to participate.
Education is not a state residence credential when permanent-visa administration disappears.
Protection against persecution is compatible with unrestricted human association.
Cultural-origin discrimination perpetuates national hierarchy.
Everyone shares need-based provision, but noncitizen welfare and social-housing eligibility are superseded categories.
Cultural difference itself should neither advantage nor disadvantage movement.

axes.brief: With national and class antagonisms overcome, permanent war-making states and standing armies lose their purpose.
axes.counterEvidence: Transitional armed revolution is outside the scoped higher-phase end-state and cannot supply its military policy.

answers.rationale: A war-making national interest is incompatible with common human association.
Negotiation fits noncoercive coordination of disagreements.
Competing military superiority would reintroduce national antagonism.
A permanent state preemptive-war entitlement is outside the peaceful end-state.
Shared protection is possible, but state alliances and war powers are not permanent institutions.
Compulsory national service contradicts the end of the military state.
Peaceful accommodation outweighs an obsolete competitive national position.
Autonomous national weapons reproduce coercive war-making.
Protection of people is legitimate, but national defence establishments are superseded.
The higher-phase ideal envisages peaceful association rather than armed interstate alliance duties.
Expeditionary warfare is incompatible with dissolved national antagonisms.
Disputes should be managed without starting wars.
Military threats recreate domination between peoples.
Avoiding war outweighs military prestige.
Interstate military espionage perpetuates rival national war systems.
Reducing military capabilities fits the end of coercive rivalry.

axes.brief: International human association supersedes competing national sovereignties, but no coercive world state is substituted.
axes.counterEvidence: Engels’s replacement of government by administration is counter-evidence to interpreting internationalism as a binding global sovereign.

answers.rationale: Exclusive national sovereignty contradicts international human association.
Shared administration is desirable but coercive international government is not substituted for the national state.
Both national and international sovereign courts are superseded.
Durable cooperation is supported, compulsory state alliances are not permanent institutions.
Voluntary association permits change, but withdrawal by a national government is an obsolete institutional premise.
Accountability is necessary without prescribing sovereign courts over governments.
National advantage cannot override the common conditions of human life.
Ecological coordination is necessary but coercive supranational state authority is not assumed.
Cooperation need not be a bloc of states with binding foreign-policy discipline.
Human freedom is central, but institutional commands to national law presume states absent from this scope.
Neither national nor international monetary sovereignty remains essential once commodity exchange is superseded.
Pooled resources and common decisions are compatible with shared administration.
Exclusive state border control contradicts the stateless ideal.
Common distribution is supported while national trade-rule systems are superseded.
International association is favoured but an enduring political federation of coercive states is not.
Cooperative rule-following is possible, but interstate enforcement is not the higher-phase mechanism.

axes.brief: Common productive resources are neither private capitalist property nor ownership by a permanent government. Literal public/private questions often fit neither alternative.
axes.counterEvidence: IEP distinguishes social and state ownership. Rejecting both ownership choices yields neutral comparisons; no government is relabelled a commune.

answers.rationale: Private capitalist ownership contradicts common productive resources.
Socially held utilities are neither government property nor private capital.
Comparable cost does not justify private productive appropriation.
Common production supersedes both government commercial firms and private competitive firms.
Privately owned healthcare production contradicts common provision.
Rail resources are common, not property of a permanent government.
Private contracting would restore capitalist productive control.
Neither public nor private banking is the organising basis of noncommodity production.
Sale to private capital contradicts social ownership.
Common access to housing is neither state landlordism nor private rental ownership.
Regulatory security does not justify capitalist strategic ownership.
Common resources are not the same as state-owned extraction businesses.
Private waste-service contracts restore a form of production the ideal supersedes.
Common strategic resources remain social, but government ownership and sale revenue are obsolete categories.
Private sale cannot be the answer to common production difficulties.
Common communications need not take either state-broadcaster or private-owner form.

axes.brief: Commodity exchange and competing national capital are superseded. Tariff rivalry and unrestricted capitalist trade are both outside the ideal.
axes.counterEvidence: Public needs still require international coordination, but this is not market trade in the question’s ordinary meaning.

answers.rationale: National tariffs to protect capital are inconsistent with common production.
Unhindered social distribution is favoured, but capitalist trade liberalisation is not the higher-phase institution.
National supplier preference conflicts with common human provisioning.
Shared sourcing serves need, not independent firms choosing capitalist bargains.
Coercive national import restrictions are not the means of provisioning.
National trade barriers and unilateral tariff bargaining both cease as institutions.
Incubating national capitalist industry is outside the end-state.
Domestic and foreign private investment are equally superseded.
Common food production should not be fenced by national import privilege.
Neither exposed capitalist competition nor state protection describes social allocation.
Retaliatory tariff rivalry recreates antagonism between national economies.
Product-tax parity and discriminatory product taxes are both outside noncommodity distribution.
Rival government-subsidy restrictions do not structure common production.
Shared supply is supported but tariff treaties are not the organising mechanism.
Neither foreign nor domestic capital should privately control strategic resources.
Access to useful services is free of national barriers, but commercial purchase remains an obsolete premise.

axes.brief: Society consciously organises production for use, but not through a permanent coercive government directing private firms.
axes.counterEvidence: Planning in the ideal is real, yet the axis specifies government versus market decisions. Several neutral responses flag that both mechanisms are superseded.

answers.rationale: Independent capitalist output decisions conflict with common production.
Social production has a plan, but compulsory government targets for firms are not its stateless form.
Commodity supply-and-demand pricing is superseded by production for use.
Common allocation of investment is not direction by a permanent national government.
Production should satisfy need rather than solvent market demand.
Common essentials are distributed by need rather than either government prices or seller pricing.
Private market entry and government permission to form firms both assume superseded institutions.
Neither government-directed nor private lending structures common production.
Capital mobility and governmental capital permissions are both superseded.
Social allocation directs development without subsidies to private industries.
Rival private currencies contradict noncommodity common provisioning.
Need-based provision replaces both negotiated low wages and a legal wage floor.
Employer bargaining and government wage schedules are both superseded by associated labour.
Public central-bank planning is a transitional mechanism, not the higher phase.
Market rents conflict with common access to shelter.
Associated planning is supported but government command over firms is not silently relabelled as common administration.

axes.brief: Provision by need supersedes wage incomes and redistributive cash taxes. The survey’s fiscal mechanism is not equivalent to the communist distribution principle.
axes.counterEvidence: Midpoint fiscal scores here do not mean moderate redistribution: the income-and-tax premise is absent because distribution is organised directly by need.

answers.rationale: Direct provision by need supersedes income redistribution through taxes and benefits.
Retaining unequal private income is not a principle of the communist end-state.
Need is met collectively rather than through a taxable cash-benefit minimum.
A survival-only floor falls short of development and need-based provision.
High and low taxable earnings are superseded rather than assigned permanent tax schedules.
Unequal private earnings do not outrank common need.
Private large inheritances are superseded, not retained as a fiscal transfer base.
Need does not cease when a fixed benefit period expires.
Accumulated private wealth and cash-transfer taxation are superseded together.
Minimising support to protect taxpayer wealth contradicts provision by need.
Common provision should enable full individual and social development.
Tax cuts versus cash-benefit expansion is outside the end-state’s distributive institutions.
Low wages and income supplements disappear as distribution is organised by need.
Permanent marginal income-tax classes are not retained.
Common land is preferred to either concentrated estates or compensated private subdivision.
Restricting provision to destitution conflicts with meeting everyone’s developmental needs.

axes.brief: No state or clerical rule remains; conscience is private and social knowledge is not governed by revelation.
axes.counterEvidence: The absence of the state does not imply mandatory private atheism or suppression of believers.

answers.rationale: Shared decisions require worldly social reasons rather than revelation.
No religious body should supply binding law over others.
Common affairs should be free of clerical approval.
A religious constitution would restore a state hierarchy.
Open study of religion is compatible with free intellectual development.
A state’s effort to cultivate an official faith is incompatible with free association.
Civil and religious state-court systems are both superseded, without granting clerics authority.
Clerical legislative review would reintroduce privileged rule.
Shared civic activity need not endorse organised worship.
Coercively funded religious propagation conflicts with voluntary conscience.
Common institutions should not endorse a single creed.
Inherited festivals may be voluntary, but official religious privilege is rejected.
Reserved clerical government seats have no place in a stateless association.
Both special religious tax exemptions and an ordinary state tax code are superseded.
Personal unions should not depend on religious permission.
Coercively binding religious family rulings contradict free association.

axes.brief: Free individual development and changed social relations displace bourgeois family hierarchy; exact modern intimate institutions are not prescribed.
axes.counterEvidence: Classical emancipation does not establish documented views on present-day marriage law, abortion or identity terminology. Conditional modelling is explicitly distinguished from historical advocacy.

answers.rationale: Changing social relations opens customs to substantial transformation.
Past practice does not bind emancipated individuals.
Free development supports family forms beyond bourgeois property norms.
Fixed hierarchical sex roles conflict with overcoming imposed division.
Free unions are compatible with equality, but state marriage classification is not prescribed.
One inherited household form cannot govern everyone’s free development.
Bodily autonomy and responsibilities toward reproduction require free social judgement rather than a fixed classical rule.
Inherited family ideology should not monopolise social education.
Caring relationships matter, but the ideal does not prescribe a state adoption classification.
Public dress should not be controlled by inherited moral authority.
Forms of address can evolve voluntarily, without a compulsory universal convention.
Collective transformation need not preserve prior class society’s moral codes.
Overcoming imposed social roles supports acceptance of varied adult lives.
Fundamental emancipation is not bound to gradual institutional change.
Shared education can discuss human diversity without a prescribed state curriculum.
Freely chosen historical customs can persist without an obligation to preserve them.

axes.brief: Abundant productive capacity supports human development, with conscious management rather than capitalist compulsion; specific high-risk inventions require judgement.
axes.counterEvidence: SEP describes disagreement over productivist and ecological Marx. Neither reckless innovation nor universal technological prohibition follows.

answers.rationale: Productive advance and conscious protection of human development require case-specific balance.
Neither permanent restriction nor universal early release follows from associated production.
Common infrastructure needs and ecological reproduction both count.
Common health requires meaningful scientific safety assessment.
With livelihood detached from wages, labour-saving tools can release time for development.
Habitats sustain life, while essential common production can also justify change.
Food innovation is judged by need and ecological effects, not novelty alone.
Nontherapeutic irreversible implants warrant substantial evidence.
Common environmental care can combine technical change with altered consumption.
Poorly understood irreversible ecological loss justifies further study.
Free development permits interest in enhancement while common safety cautions against premature use.
Reliable medicine requires evidence about different recipients.
Developing capacities and protecting future persons leave enhancement trials conditional.
Common dependence on ecosystems supports evidence before wide cultivation.
Shelter and movement are real needs alongside ecological continuity.
Conscious social control should avoid irreversible harm unsupported by good evidence.

axes.brief: Administration coordinates shared production without a central or regional coercive state. Voluntary scale is not an automatic localism rule.
axes.counterEvidence: Large-scale coordination can coexist with local administration. Neither an enduring national government nor regional sovereign mini-states is the ideal.

answers.rationale: Regional state rights and national override are both superseded by association.
A sovereign national final say would restore political hierarchy.
Voluntary association permits regrouping, but a state-secession referendum is not the ideal’s necessary form.
Coercive national override contradicts disappearance of rule over persons.
Local organisation can vary without constitutions for sovereign regional governments.
A single national police command is incompatible with the end-state.
Local retention versus national allocation of tax revenue assumes a tax state absent here.
Coercive national curriculum command is not free intellectual association.
Competing regional tax rates and uniform state rates are both superseded.
Common labour arrangements replace state employment law over employers.
Communities should shape their administrative arrangements voluntarily.
Shared healthcare allocation is required but national-government coverage decrees are not assumed.
Indigenous communities can organise local affairs without imposed state authority.
Neither regional tax competition nor national tax policing structures common provision.
Locally confined ecological administration can be locally organised.
Shared emergency coordination is necessary without compelling communities through a sovereign national command.

axes.brief: Gotha combines transformed social development with distinct natural abilities and needs; social emancipation is not biological uniformity.
axes.counterEvidence: Gotha explicitly recognises natural endowment; social transformation should not be confused with a claim that all individual variation is socially caused.

answers.rationale: Transformed social relations are expected to reshape everyday behaviour.
Historical materialism stresses social development while Gotha recognises differing natural endowments; together these do not fix the causal majority behind present-day country IQ differences.
The transformed division of labour changes socially organised gender conduct.
Different embodied needs and conditions both affect stress responses.
Access to varied activity enables new interests and developed powers.
Individual disposition and experience remain relevant in risk-taking.
Associated production cultivates cooperation without denying human capacities for it.
Shared life develops concern while individual endowments can still differ.
Abundant education can develop attention without eliminating biological variation.
Historical moral consciousness changes with social relations rather than remaining biologically fixed.
Non-antagonistic surroundings should change learned perceptions of threat.
Abolishing class does not abolish individual temperamental differences or their development.
Changing culture and embodied attraction can coexist in free association.
Removing antagonistic social conditions is more consistent than racial biological explanations of violence.
Learning and common life are more relevant than inherited racial self-control claims.

The ideal supersedes wage-market valuation; its historical account of household and productive labour nevertheless favours socially organised work over sex differences in productive contribution as the main explanation of existing pay gaps.

review.notes: Read all 240 answers against the current question wording and checked values, rationales, cited source IDs and axis distinctions. Checked the higher-phase scope against Gotha, Engels and SEP/IEP. Audited every state-ownership, planning, wage and tax premise: explicit rejection-of-both neutral responses are questionnaire-fit limitations, not support for private ownership or evidence of political moderation. Did not silently rename the state as a commune. Clarified Culture02 and reduced the pay-gap claim to a modest historical-structural inference. No incumbent government is claimed to instantiate the stateless ideal. All answers remain labelled inferred: these are scoped representative models, not claimed questionnaire responses or empirical measurements of adherents. Review used no target scores or similarity tuning. Similarity audit remains the catalogue coordinator’s separate step.
